gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker Prime 200W (A2683), the pick in most of the chats, cannot hold 100 W + 100 W indefinitely. Under a constant 2 × 100 W electronic load, techtest.org saw it interrupt the load and throttle to 70 W per port after about 1.5 hours. In the same tester's 2 × 100 W (20 V/5 A) run, the UGREEN Nexode 200W desktop (CD271) held the load for about 6 hours.
standout_why: I compared against these cited or top results: anker.com A2683 and the Anker service spec page, Macworld's Anker Prime 250W review (Simon Jary, 2024-08-30), Android Authority's best-chargers roundup (Robert Triggs, 2025-11-27), computingforgeeks' Real Port Splits, and our own page. None of them reports sustained-load behaviour for the A2683. Anker's pages give only 'each can deliver up to 100W' and a general line about 'adjusting power output' with temperature. Macworld and Android Authority say nothing about throttling or heat on the 200W. Computingforgeeks mentions derating only for the Prime 160W. Our page notes throttling only for the Prime 250W. The 5 A / e-marked cable point does not count as new: anker.com ('use E-Marker chip cables'), computingforgeeks and our page all already state it.
decides: This confirms the A2683 for ordinary use: the tester himself says 100–150 W is sustainable long-term and 'in der Praxis ... kein Drama', because laptop charging tapers. It qualifies the pick for a shopper whose two laptops draw a full 100 W for hours, such as heavy workloads while plugged in. For that shopper the page should say the A2683 drops to 70 W per port after about 1.5 h, and that the UGREEN CD271 desktop, in the only like-for-like test found (same reviewer and method), held 2 × 100 W for about 6 h. For the UGREEN 200W 4-port wall charger, the page should name which hardware revision it links: Notebookcheck reports customer complaints of heat and erratic output on the original, and UGREEN has released a revised unit.

findings.label: Maker's description of the throttling mechanism
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (200W, 6 Port, GaN) – Anker service product description
findings.note: Anker says ActiveShield 3.0 works by 'intelligently monitoring temperature and adjusting power output'. The page gives no thresholds and no derating curve. Its per-port spec is 20.0V⎓5.0A, 100.0W on USB-C1 to C4, and 'Two Ports in Use: Up to 200.0W Max'.

findings.label: Sustained 2 × 100 W load (measured)
findings.value: Held 2 × 100 W for about 1.5 h, then throttled to 70 W per port
findings.source_title: Anker Prime 200W Ladegerät im Test: High-End Power für alle Geräte? (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2024-07-25)
findings.note: Method: two electronic loads at a constant 2 × 100 W. Verbatim: 'Nach rund 1,5 Stunden unterbrach das Ladegerät den Entladevorgang und drosselte sich auf je 70 W pro Port.' Barton's judgement: '100–150 W schafft das Gerät praktisch aber dauerhaft.' and 'in der Praxis ist dies aber auch kein Drama.' He describes the outside of the case as not very hot. The article does not say which two ports were loaded. 70 W per port means 140 W total, against 200 W before throttling.

findings.label: Sustained 2 × 100 W load (measured)
findings.value: About 6 h at 200 W (2 × 100 W at 20 V/5 A) with no failure
findings.source_title: Das UGREEN Nexode 200W USB C Ladegerät im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2023-03-27)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'Ich habe das UGREEN Nexode 200W ca. 6 Stunden mit 200W (2x 100W / 20V/5A) belastet.' and 'Dies hat das Ladegerät auch problemlos überstanden.' Caveat: the article notes this run had fans nearby and gives no temperature figure. The CD271 is the 4× USB-C + 2× USB-A desktop unit, the 'UGREEN Nexode 6-Port 200W' card ChatGPT showed from Best Buy. It is not the 4-port wall charger.

findings.label: Hardware revision and reported faults
findings.value: Original (ASIN B0DG91Q6YD): customers reported 'high temperature and erratic power outputs'. Revised version (ASIN B0G7HZT7DN): $99.99 RRP
findings.source_title: New upgraded Ugreen 200W 4-port Charger coming to US (Notebookcheck, Polly Allcock, 2026-05-11)
findings.note: Notebookcheck is reporting customer complaints here, not its own measurements. It says the new edition is 'supposed to tackle the issues with the first model' and that the first two USB-C ports charge two laptops at 100 W each. The original was $59.99 for Prime members at the time. The manuals.plus PDF ChatGPT cited (B0DG91Q6YD) is the original revision.

findings.note: On the A2683, Android Authority notes only that it 'scores very good efficiency' and says nothing about heat or stability. Macworld's Prime 250W review (https://www.macworld.com/article/2438907/anker-prime-charger-review.html, read 2026-11-13) has no throttling or heat statement.
